title: Reflected on the tad/git-subrepo work and proposed a fork-based package manager
done: After building and battle-testing the tad/git-subrepo system, proposed a different but related system: fork each dependency into an owned repo, add an additive file structure, and automate the fork/sync/patch-back loop. Researched prior art first rather than assuming it was novel.
considered: Continuing to extend the tad/subrepo approach itself for third-party dependencies.
rejected: tad/subrepo solves "distribute code we originate across our own repos" - a different problem from "own and patch code we do not originate." Kept both rather than merging them.

title: Rejected the name "gita" for a naming collision
done: Checked before committing to the name and found nosarthur/gita (1,600+ stars, popular, active) already exists as an unrelated multi-repo git CLI tool.

title: Named the project Rhizoid, offshoots rhizoid-cuttings (rhizcut)
done: "Rhizoid" was picked from the Rhizome ecosystem - the literal botanical term for "resembles a rhizome, simpler," matching the stated framing of this project as a simpler offshoot of Rhizome. Checked for collisions before committing (none found). Individual managed dependencies are "rhizoid-cuttings" (rhizcut), from the horticultural cutting - a piece rooted separately from its parent, independent from then on.

title: Upgraded rustnix into a proper template before generating rhizoid from it
done: Added CI (fmt/clippy/test/doc/MSRV), release-plz + cliff.toml, PR-title linting, and a tests/ scaffold to grenudi/rustnix, mirroring argenv-opencommons/argenv's proven setup, marked it as a GitHub template, then generated git-rhizoid/rhizoid from it - same sequence as text-as-data-template before software-engineering-canon.
considered: Building the CI/release setup directly in the rhizoid repo instead.
rejected: Any other future Rust project benefits from the same upgrade to rustnix, not just this one.

title: Found and fixed a real CI-breaking bug: the mold linker requirement
done: .cargo/config.toml requires the mold linker, present locally only via the Nix devshell. A bare GitHub Actions runner does not have it, so every cargo build/test in CI, and release-plz's own package verification, would have failed. Fixed by installing mold explicitly in both ci.yml and release-plz.yml - found by actually running the CI steps locally with a real toolchain and by watching a real release attempt fail, not by review.

title: Found and fixed Dependabot silently defeating the MSRV job
done: Dependabot opened a real PR within minutes of rustnix going live, proposing dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.75.0 -> @1.120.0 in the msrv job - it cannot tell a version pinned as a floor to test against from a version to keep current. Closed the PR without merging and added a Dependabot ignore rule.

title: Removed publish = false too early, then restored it
done: Removed publish = false from rhizoid's Cargo.toml on the assumption a real project should be publishable from the start. A real release attempt then correctly tried to publish an empty v0.1.0 (src/main.rs has no real functionality yet) and failed on a missing CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. Restored publish = false - crates.io has no true delete, only yank, so publishing a placeholder was the wrong call regardless of the token.
considered: Adding a CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret to make the failed publish succeed.
rejected: That would have published a genuinely empty crate under the real "rhizoid" name - the missing token was not the actual problem.

title: Adopted the RFC-like minimal style from text-as-data-template
done: Pulled the definition-list render.py change via git subrepo pull (clean, no conflicts, this repo uses the stock engine renderer directly) and added the matching _config.yml, _layouts/default.html and assets/css/style.css by hand, since those are not vendored - adapted from text-as-data-template with this repo's own title and description.
considered: Waiting for someone to ask for it here specifically, since it was originally scoped to the template repo only.
rejected: The whole point of building this system was that engine improvements should be easy to bring in - proving that immediately, on real repos, mattered more than waiting.

title: Researched prior art before designing the v1 command surface
done: Looked specifically at how mature tools handle three things this design needed: a destination that varies per managed item rather than being hardcoded (west's manifest: a named remotes list, each project can override which one it uses - see [fork-destination-manifest](concepts.md#fork-destination-manifest)), detecting when reality has drifted from a recorded manifest (Terraform's plan / drift detection: the state file is a record of intent, not a source of truth to trust blindly - see [drift-detection](concepts.md#drift-detection)), and adopting something that already exists instead of always creating new (Terraform's import, kept as a separate command from apply precisely because the two operations have different blast radii - see [adopt-vs-create](concepts.md#adopt-vs-create)). All three map directly onto Rhizoid's stated requirements: per-project fork destination, a CLI that checks real git state rather than only the manifest, and a way to point at an existing satisfactory fork without creating a duplicate.

title: Settled the v1 command surface and the fork's own metadata file
done: Seven verbs for v1 (see [rhizoid-command-surface](concepts.md#rhizoid-command-surface)): init, add, import, update, status, refresh, remove. send-upstream (clean patch back to the true upstream) is real and designed but deferred to v0.2, after the core loop is proven on real dependencies. Each managed fork carries its own .rhizoid/module.toml (see [module-metadata-file](concepts.md#module-metadata-file)), mirroring .tad/.gitrepo's pattern already proven in the tad system: a plain, readable file is the source of truth for a module's state, not something buried in commit messages or a separate database.
considered: A single add command with a flag choosing create-vs-adopt behavior, and folding status and a Terraform-style separate plan into one command.
rejected: A flag with a default is exactly the kind of thing that goes wrong quietly - kept add and import as separate verbs instead, matching Terraform's own precedent (see [adopt-vs-create](concepts.md#adopt-vs-create)). Folding plan into status was kept, though: unlike cloud infrastructure, inspecting local git state and GitHub's API is cheap and side-effect-free, so there is no real cost to always doing it - no need for a separate read-only-vs-mutating split the way Terraform needs one.

title: Kept the consumption-side manifest deferred, distinct from this plan
done: This plan covers the fork-management side only: how Rhizoid forks, tracks, and syncs dependencies into a configured org. How a third repo (something that is not Rhizoid itself) declares "I depend on this org's fork of X at version Y" and pulls it in remains a separate, undesigned problem, kept apart on purpose since the first reflection on this project.

title: Decided the manifest format (TOML) and that auth goes through gh for now
done: Researched the JSON/YAML/TOML tradeoffs specifically for a hand-editable, cross-language project manifest rather than a deeply nested orchestration config (see [manifest-file-format](concepts.md#manifest-file-format)): TOML's comment support and lack of YAML's implicit-typing and indentation footguns fit a manifest people edit by hand, and its array-of-tables syntax matches "a list of modules" directly. Found and weighed the honest counter-case before committing: Cloudflare's Wrangler moved away from TOML-only specifically over its array-of-tables footgun in a heavily hand-edited config - judged as a smaller risk here because the manifest is meant to be edited through add/import/remove rather than freehand, and per-module detail lives in each fork's own .rhizoid/module.toml rather than in one large top-level file (see [distributed-state-no-lockfile](concepts.md#distributed-state-no-lockfile)). Also decided, separately and far more simply: auth goes through an already-authenticated gh for now (see [auth-via-gh](concepts.md#auth-via-gh)), rather than Rhizoid managing its own credentials.
considered: JSON/JSONC for the manifest, matching Wrangler's own current recommendation.
rejected: JSONC is not a real standard (every parser's comment-stripping behavior differs slightly) and lacks TOML's native date/array-of-tables types; the footgun that pushed Wrangler away from TOML applies less here given how the manifest is actually meant to be edited.

title: Read argenv's real source before designing the boundary layer around it
done: Fetched argenv's actual API (Input/Arg/Env, the resolve/lint functions) and argenv-cli's own main.rs rather than assuming a clap-like shape from its one-line description. Found it declares flags and environment variables only - no subcommands, no positional arguments (see [argenv-is-flags-and-env-only](concepts.md#argenv-is-flags-and-env-only)). Settled the boundary layer's shape on that basis: a two-crate workspace, rhizoid-core and rhizoid-cli (see [rhizoid-crate-shape](concepts.md#rhizoid-crate-shape)), a hand-written verb dispatcher matching argenv-cli's own reference pattern, argenv Models for each command's named flags (with env fallback, so CI/scripts can drive Rhizoid without touching argv at all), and manifest infrastructure (Manifest/Module types, TOML read/write, a schemars-derived schema, a schema subcommand mirroring argenv-cli's own). The real git/gh operations behind GitPort/GitHubPort are explicitly out of scope for this pass - each command resolves and validates its inputs and loads the manifest, and either does the one thing that needs no GitHub (init) or reports plainly that the rest is not implemented yet.
considered: Assuming argenv worked like a typical CLI-parsing crate (subcommands, positional arguments) from its description alone.
rejected: Would have produced a design that does not compile against the real crate. Reading the actual source first cost a handful of API calls and avoided building the wrong thing.

title: Implemented the boundary layer: manifest infra, 7 argenv-typed commands, 39 tests
done: Two-crate workspace in git-rhizoid/rhizoid (rhizoid-core, rhizoid-cli - see [rhizoid-crate-shape](concepts.md#rhizoid-crate-shape)). init and remove are fully working, needing no GitHub; the other five (add, import, update, status, refresh) resolve and validate their inputs against a real argenv Model, then report plainly that they are not implemented yet rather than pretending to work. Verified locally and on real GitHub Actions, including the MSRV job.

title: Three real bugs found by building and running this, not by review
done: Guessed the resolved-invocation type was called Resolved from the README's variable naming; it is actually Resolution. Model::problems() was dead code from the plain binary's perspective even with a passing test calling it, since #[cfg(test)] code is not compiled into that target at all - fixed by having main() call it as a genuine startup self-check on each command's own contract, which is itself consistent with [drift-detection](concepts.md#drift-detection) (verify, do not just trust). A stable-resolved indexmap version needed edition2024, which the declared MSRV (1.75.0) cannot parse; pinned it explicitly and, in fixing this, found Cargo.lock was gitignored (inherited from the rustnix template's generic default) - fixed to be tracked, since a binary crate needs its lockfile committed for an MSRV pin to survive a fresh clone or CI run at all.

title: Rhizoid joins the Open Commons Observatory
done: Joined with ocoeco init: the mark, the gatherer's caller; the design log's own tables (concepts, backlog, session log) shared as they are, and a path written only from the backlog - the command line, the consumption side, a TUI - whose last stop reads ocoeco's own backlog: ocoeco travelling as a rhizcut.
considered: Writing milestones the backlog does not hold.
rejected: That: the path says what the project's own records show.

title: Its idea, told for anyone
done: The idea of Rhizoid written as an ordered piece of writing in its own data - borrowed versus owned, a cutting rather than a copy, nothing hidden, what it does not fix, where it stands - for a reader who knows nothing of it.
considered: Terse cards of concepts.
rejected: Those as the idea: they name the parts for an insider.

title: Its workings, told
done: What delivers and proves the steps reached so far - the design log, the declarations layer and its tests - written under the steps they serve. The TUI and carrying ocoeco are left with nothing under them.
considered: Filling every step.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves should be seen.

title: tad in Rust replaces the vendored Python engine
done: This repository moved to tad in Rust: tables.toml is the authority, tad comes from its pinned release, the vendored .tad, schema.sql, load.sql and checks/ are gone, and AGENTS.md got simpler. The open item about dc.py blocking recovery from an empty table closed with it.

title: A concept's text is its summary
done: The concepts table's statement field is now summary, the word the shared language (ocoeco's language.toml) and twenty other projects use; the observatory showed this repository's concepts without their text because of it. Found by checking every project against the shared language.
considered: Teaching the shared language a second word for the same thing.
rejected: That: one role, one word.

title: Scope from linux-phone-oco's graph research: the follow tool for every edge, status first, by conformance
done: A research lead of linux-phone-oco measured its repository graph (12 edges, 3 moved by a job, 6 by hand, 5 behind) and the world (no Rust or shell tool carries root-level files down and changes up; only copybara, on a JVM; josh needs a monorepo; subtree/subrepo need a prefix - the tad/subrepo lesson of 2026-09-22 again). It filed status-over-every-edge and follow-by-conformance here and reshaped slice-consumption, followers-one-pin-bump, send-back-writes-the-upstream-item and implement-cli to that order (source linux-phone-oco-base-graph).
considered: Porting idealkb's follow.sh into rhizoid now; rhizoid as a template engine; rows as an edge kind.
rejected: A port before conformance (the shell works and is tested); a template engine or a merge of data (bases are data); rows (docs' feeds own them).

title: git-rhizoid unparked by the author's yes: the follow tool for every edge, in the research's order
done: The author's word, verbatim (through the Top Coordinator, 2026-11-18, recorded in linux-phone-oco/docs as session-log 2026-11-18-author-yes-device-layer-and-rhizoid): 'yes, if its the best we came up with, grounded in our extensive research and consideration, which it seems it did, so yes'. It unparks implement-cli with the scope of 2026-11-18-scope-every-edge and its order, now the backlog's rank: 1 status-over-every-edge (passes graph-drift.sh), 2 follow-by-conformance (passes idealkb's bin/test-follow.sh, keeping the pin names its source, one owner per file, the followers-answer gate), 3-4 slice-consumption and followers-one-pin-bump, 5 send-back, 6-7 cuttings (rhizcut, cutting-as-cargo-dependency). Owner: git-rhizoid-builder, who keeps AGENTS.md's Owner line here and in git-rhizoid/rhizoid. Each step replaces shell only once it passes; idealkb's update-pins and follow.sh stay until step 2 passes.
considered: Unparking only status and leaving the rest parked; ranking only the first two.
rejected: Leaving the order in notes: the rank is a field now, so the next builder reads it rather than infers it.

title: A decisions table, and its first row: the standard tools - drive, cut, or write
done: Added a decisions table to tables.toml (shaped like linux-phone-oco/docs' decisions; id in unique_ids) and recorded decision 2026-11-23-standard-tools-drive-cut-or-write on the author's direction of 2026-11-23, weighed by the rhizoid lane coordinator: drive the git CLI for worktree and rerere, drive git and the kernel's own tools rather than b4. Sources gitoxide, git2-rs and git-rerere added.
considered: Each tool three ways: drive the CLI, a rhizcut used as a library, our own.
rejected: Recording the decision as a session_log row only: a decision with what was rejected is its own table, as in linux-phone-oco/docs.

title: The structure's git flows run on rhizoid: assemble and kernel status ranked first
done: Landed the needs agreed by the rhizoid lane coordinator with the Steward, after linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid: decisions 2026-11-23-rhizoid-carries-the-structure-git-flows and 2026-11-23-structure-flows-ranked-first; new backlog rows assemble-from-list (rank 2), status-over-kernel-edges (rank 3), gix-worktree-add-upstream (unranked); send-back-writes-the-upstream-item (4) and followers-one-pin-bump (5) reshaped, their old text kept; follow-by-conformance, slice-consumption, rhizcut, cutting-as-cargo-dependency re-ranked 6-9. Data only; no code until the coordinator relays that work may resume.
considered: The unpark order of 2026-11-18; the merge loop kept in lab-tools.
rejected: As in the two decisions' rejected fields.

title: rhizoid assemble released in v0.1.1
done: Built backlog assemble-from-list in git-rhizoid/rhizoid (PR #12, released as v0.1.1 by PR #10): rhizoid assemble LIST reads a lab's list file, which rhizoid owns (examples/topics.toml), and merges the list onto its base in a fresh locked worktree under AGENT_WORKTREES/REPO/rhizoid, with git's shared rerere. It stops at a conflict and names the earlier entries that changed the same paths. It tags int/DEVICE/LIST/BASE/N with the recipe; --reproduces compares the trees and --fetch prunes. Git is driven through GitPort (decision 2026-11-23-standard-tools-drive-cut-or-write). A programmer review before landing found seven points; all were fixed before the merge.
considered: Persisting rerere.autoUpdate in the clone's config; refusing a local branch behind origin's.
rejected: autoUpdate in the clone's config (it would stage rerere's replays in a person's own merges; rhizoid passes it per run); refusing stale local branches (unpushed local work is common on a kernel clone; the recipe names the sha that went in, and the README says so).

title: rhizoid v0.2.0: status over integration edges; assemble ends worktrees, reuses unchanged tags, and stays general
done: Landed git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #13, released as v0.2.0 (PR #14). Backlog status-over-kernel-edges is done, as general [[integration]] edges. Also in it: the Steward's check of assemble v0.1.1 (--done TAG [--force]; a conflict leaves the worktree unlocked; an unchanged recipe is its tag; tested_commit a commit's sha), the ikb record keys, and decision 2026-11-23-rhizoid-stays-general (--lists required; the list file names its tag template and branch patterns; device is read as name). Three programmer reviews before landing; every point fixed. The send-back row now carries ikb upstream-item's field names.
considered: A kernel profile kept as a default; persisting rerere.autoUpdate; refusing every local branch that differs from origin's.
rejected: As in decision 2026-11-23-rhizoid-stays-general; flagging stale local branches in status (branch-origin) rather than refusing them in assemble, since unpushed local work is common.

title: rhizoid send-back released in v0.2.1
done: Built backlog send-back-writes-the-upstream-item in git-rhizoid/rhizoid (PR #15, released as v0.2.1 by PR #16), general like assemble: send and tag names, checks and recipients are rhizoid's config, the kernel's are an example. A programmer review before landing found seven points, all fixed: a run that cannot finish keeps nothing; no other branch moves; an empty series is refused; dropped commits are counted; a person's format.* config does not reach the series; the recipients command's failure fails the run.
considered: Running checks through a shell; leaving a conflicted send worktree for a hand; a built-in list of checkpatch exceptions.
rejected: A shell (argv only: a config is not a script); keeping a conflicted send branch (the fix belongs on the topic branch, so nothing is kept); built-in exceptions (they are the check's own arguments, in config).

title: rhizoid v0.2.2: send-back drafts; status asks origin and the releases source
done: Landed git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #17 (status: branch-origin asks origin with ls-remote, so a clone tracking one branch still answers; an integration edge names its releases source and topic-base is not-known-yet without one; remote asks never hang or prompt; a shallow clone's missing release is not-known-yet) and PR #19 (send-back drafts, as the send-back row says), released as v0.2.2 (PR #18). Each was reviewed by the programmer subagent before landing, every point fixed.
considered: A --sent SHA flag to mark a version sent now; counting local-only topics as drift.
rejected: --sent now (marking a version sent stays the author's one manual step until he wants it); local-only topics as drift (unpushed work is normal; status names them without failing).

title: rhizoid v0.2.3: bump keeps every pin in one place; every release carries its binary
done: Landed git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #20 (assets.yml: the x86_64 Linux binary and its sha256 attached to every release, as lab-tools does; dispatched for v0.2.2 and checked by download, sha256 -c and a run) and PR #22 (rhizoid bump, backlog followers-one-pin-bump), released as v0.2.3 (PR #21). A programmer review found eight points, all fixed: a pushed branch survives a failed pull request; one pin's error is its row's; the commit is the pin alone; the edit proves nothing else moved; --push and --pr need now.
considered: toml_edit for key pins; bumping slices too.
rejected: toml_edit (a line edit proven by parsing the whole file against the original with the one key set is enough, with no new dependency); slices (their files are laid by follow, rank 6).

title: rhizoid v0.2.5: follow lays a slice as idealkb's follow.sh does, byte for byte
done: Landed git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #25 (rhizoid follow, backlog follow-by-conformance), released as v0.2.5 (PR #26); and before it PR #23, v0.2.4: a [[tool]] names in also what its gate may change (a Cargo.lock), committed with the pin. Sent orchestration the [[tool]] TOML for the attended pins (surya-lab procedures/steps, google-walleye-lab tools/walleye-tries) with value, gate (cargo check) and also, for docs' graph.
considered: Reimplementing diff -u; a regex engine for markers; a shell agreement script.
rejected: Reimplementing diff -u (rhizoid drives diff, as it drives git); a regex engine (markers are words; a regex one is refused, on purpose); a shell script (practice 21: the agreement is a Rust test, run in CI).

title: rhizoid v0.2.6: bump moves slice pins through follow; rhizcut designed, waiting for its read
done: Wrote slice-consumption's remainder against follow and built it: bump now moves a [[slice]] pin through rhizoid follow on a branch, gated (git-rhizoid/rhizoid PR #27, v0.2.6 by PR #28; a programmer review's five points fixed: the commit is what follow laid, nothing outside the follower, owner-repo branch names, the graph's pin proven moved). Recorded decision 2026-11-23-pins-stay-with-their-readers (no follower-wide pin file), split generic-file-back into its own row, and wrote rhizcut's design into its row for the coordinator's read before building.
considered: One pin file for every kind; building rhizcut before its design was read.
rejected: As the decision says; building first (rhizcut forks on GitHub: outward, the design goes first and the first real fork waits for the author).

title: rhizoid v0.3.0: rhizcut takes and keeps cuttings, recorded in the graph
done: Built rank 8 (rhizcut) as designed and read by the coordinator: add, import, update, refresh, remove on the graph's [[fork]] edges; GitHub only through GitHubPort's one adapter, gh; every verb a plan, outward steps marked, nothing done without now. Released as v0.3.0 (breaking: init and rhizoid.toml retired). Ran import's dry runs for linux-phone-oco/linux and sxmo-utils against docs' graph, for the author's go through the coordinator.
considered: Keeping rhizoid.toml beside the graph; pushing to origin by name.
rejected: As the decision says; origin by name (a clone's origin may be the upstream: the fork is found by its URL).

title: rhizoid v0.3.1 and v0.3.2: integration cuttings track releases; cut tags for cuttings consumed by Cargo
done: v0.3.1 (PR #31): an integration cutting records tracks = its integration's releases source, and update pushes nothing for it, reporting status's topic-base. v0.3.2 (PR #33 quoted [patch."URL"] keys, PR #35 cut tags): backlog cutting-as-cargo-dependency done - the last of the ranked backlog.
considered: Semver precedence for cut tags; reading the clone's own tags.
rejected: Semver (it would sort a cut before its release); the clone's tags (a moved upstream tag would stop every update; rhizoid reads into refs/rhizoid/ instead).

title: Research: why the author's pins condition (no drift, no busy work) was not met, and what prevents it by design
done: Looked at what is (docs' graph and rhizoid v0.3.2 on the lab machine, 2026-11-23): status counted 55 checks, 2 behind, 13 moved by hand. Four pin kinds have four different movers. Three already push by themselves, as user timers on the lab machine that land through land: idealkb-update-pins (hourly) for idealkb.toml slices, tad-update-pins (weekly) for bin/install-tad.sh, and lpoco-host-follow (15 min) for lab.toml tools.lpoco, which installs first and then lands the pin as the record of what runs (docs decision 2026-11-19-host-follows-releases, research host-conveyor). The kinds nothing runs are the [[tool]] Cargo pins (lpoco-attended in surya-lab and google-walleye-lab; walleye's is at 0.41.0 against 0.44.3) and lab.toml tools.rhizoid. Those are moved only when someone runs rhizoid bump. So pin-decision 2026-11-23-pins-stay-with-their-readers' wording, that bump is the only mover, was never true: lpoco has two possible movers (host follow and bump now). Cause 2: tools.rhizoid sat in lab.toml with no edge, and nothing compares a pin file's keys with the graph. Cause 3: status reports a follower's declared own files (idealkb.toml own with [why]) as moved by hand, 13 standing lines, while follow skips them whole (follow.sh lines 38-45 before the marker part at 51). Others: Renovate and Dependabot make behind a passing state by schedule plus automerge once the checks pass. A person sees only the PR whose check failed (Renovate automerge, scheduling; Dependabot schedule.interval). nix flake update runs from a scheduled CI job that opens a PR (update-flake-lock). Renovate finds every dependency by scanning files with managers, so a new dependency is covered without a list (Renovate managers).
considered: Make bump the one mover everywhere; a release hook in every source's CI; Renovate itself with regex managers; Dependabot; GitHub auto-merge on bump PRs; generating edges by scanning pin files; a suppress list in rhizoid for declared own files.
rejected: See decision 2026-11-23-every-pin-one-pushed-mover.

title: rhizoid v0.3.3: a moved tag is a tag-origin finding; status reads own files as declared
done: v0.3.3 (PR #36, PR #38, release PR #37). Orchestration's bug: bump --fetch stopped with an empty error when git refused to clobber a stale local tag (sxmo-utils-v1.18.1_p20261118 in lab-tools). Tags are now fetched with --porcelain and never forced; each refused tag is moved-by-hand tag-origin (tag, object here, origin's) and the fetch and report go on; every failed git call names the command and git's words (stdout when stderr is empty); --fetch needs git 2.41. Then status-reads-own: a reason in [why] makes a differing own file current; docs' graph went from 13 moved-by-hand own lines to 0. Both reviewed by the programmer subagent; the release asset checked by sha256.
considered: For a moved tag: fetch --force (rejected below); skip tags; turn each refused tag into a finding (chosen). For an own tables.toml's part: hide it whenever tables.toml is own; read it as declared only where follow leaves it whole (chosen, status agrees with follow).
rejected: fetch --force for tags: local tags are kept on purpose (assembled int/ tags are made locally) and a silent clobber would hide drift. Reading own with own_key in follow: follow is follow.sh's port byte for byte, so status asks how follow reads own instead.

title: rhizoid v0.3.4 to v0.3.8: one pushed mover per pin
done: The ranked backlog under decision 2026-11-23-every-pin-one-pushed-mover, each reviewed by the programmer subagent and released with its asset checked: v0.3.4 moved_by on edges (PR #39); v0.3.5 pin-copies, whole tag names only (PR #41); v0.3.6 bump now --land and the hourly user timer (PR #43); v0.3.7 pin-copies skips rhizoid-records files (PR #45); v0.3.8 [[pins]] table coverage and bump now ending 0 past a standing refusal (PR #47). On docs' graph pin-copies found the real copies (walleye's procedures and CI, surya's procedures/attended-session.rs).
considered: For records counted as copies: a skip list in the graph, or in rhizoid; a git attribute declared by the follower (chosen). For the hourly unit's exit: fail on any refusal; pass on a standing one status reports (chosen).
rejected: A list of record paths in rhizoid or the graph: it would live away from the files it describes. Failing the unit for a known standing finding: a red unit every hour hides a real failure.

title: rhizoid v0.3.9: rhizoid check, a graph never lands ahead of its host
